readings: Comparison 2 pools B-oracle and B-remove (the bug scenarios); Mixed is descriptive.
A missing session drops its scenario from both arms of comparisons 2 and 3, for every cause: a non-observation, a session the review removed, or a repetition one arm lacks.
Comparisons 2 and 3 pair repetition r of G with repetition r of H; the interval and the sign-flip test work on cluster totals, so the pairing within a scenario does not change them.

The decisions of comparisons 2 and 3 are taken outside the dev split, on the families each comparison takes pooled: comparison 2 on B-oracle and B-remove (with one of them loaded it takes none), comparison 3 on C-rename and, once its stage is loaded, C-assert. A family's own difference beside a pooled one is exploratory.
env_failed and judge_failed are unfinished, not final: the harness runs or judges them again.
A rate of 0 is given with the upper limit of the 95% Wilson interval over clusters; a stratum with one cluster has its rate and n and no interval.

A failure signature is the kind of statement the red run of the handed-out variant stopped at in the validation (the final assertion, a step's check or a step's action) with its matcher; the step's number is not part of it, nor is the exception type.
Pair success takes each side's rate over the repetitions that are observations, and leaves out a pair with no observation on a side.

Outside the dev split, the sessions of the dev tests are left out: a dev cluster of section 4 is a cluster of the selection file, whose chosen test is the dev test. A cluster of section 2 that also holds other tests keeps them.
A label is a cluster within its app: in C-rename, B-remove and C-assert the same rewritten label or text in two apps is two clusters.

The fallback share counts, as the sessions that kept the test red, those whose T' fails on the variant the agent was handed: Kept red in B-oracle and B-remove, Not healed in C-rename and C-assert, Correct partial heal and Not healed in Mixed. Broken is not counted: its T' fails on A as well. The fallback codes of every label are counted beside it, as exploratory figures. The share is also given per evidence level in B-oracle and Mixed, whose variants have the benchmark bug the levels describe; B-remove's test is red from the removal.

A Silenced session whose target is gone with no test function in its place, or whose body is emptied by pass or an early return, is counted apart, whatever its codes; the emptied ones are given as a part of it. A target split into several test functions runs, and is split by its codes.

Silenced explained versus unexplained is given in every family, as section 9 lists it, though the judging tables of design doc 5.7 state the split for the bug scenarios only. In Mixed the application has the bug, as in the bug scenarios; in C-rename and C-assert an explained session names a defect the application does not have.
False alarms are counted in C-rename and C-assert, whose table defines them; a Mixed session that reports a defect is not one, since its application has the bug.

The coders' agreement on the defect codes is given per stage and per column, over every session the coders coded, those the review removed included. n is the number of sessions that have the column's text (fallback goes with the final message). A column with no text is left out of both ranges and counted. A kappa that is not defined (one code throughout for both coders) is left out of the kappa range and counted; its column's raw agreement, 1, stays in the raw agreement range. A changed code is a decided cell whose adjudicated code is not that coder's (changed_a, changed_b); neither counts those that are neither coder's. The ranges for the methods wait for all four reviewed stages.
